text: This should be absolute music to 49ers fans' ears. >> Biggest thing you've learned from Mike Evans so far? >> Extremely smart and I feel like overthrowing him isn't really a thing. We saw so many catches in OTAs where he just got up with his length and the radius that he has. Um, you know, he's he's unique. He's a Hall of Famer. >> Impossible to overthrow Mike Evans. This opens up a whole realm of possibilities that we'll discuss in a bit, but first some more X receiver talk headlined by the fact that we won't spend more than 5 seconds talking about Brandon Aiyuk and his latest video. But, we will talk about Joey Bosa. Adam Schefter named the 49ers and only the 49ers as a potential destination for Joey, who's still deciding whether or not to continue his career in 2026. >> I think he's working on his golf game right now. So, I don't think he's thinking too much about football. >> Now, Schefter did speculate that it's likely Joey Bosa has taken his final NFL snap, but I view this a little differently. I see Joey Bosa being in Eric Kendricks' mode right now. Remember the star linebacker last year toward the tail end of his NFL career, didn't sign with the 49ers until late in the season. And he was very happy that he did. In fact, Kendricks the other day was just lauding Kyle Shanahan's team culture once again. >> I remember Shanahan came to the front of the meeting room and was like, "Hey, I don't really know you that well, Eric." Like, he called me in front in front of the whole meeting room. He's like, "I don't really know you that well, but I know that you I played against you a ton and I respect you and like you're going to handle business for us like this week." >> Joey Bosa has already put a lot of money into the bank. He's gotten married this offseason. There should be no rush for him to join an NFL team for training camp or even for the early part of the season, especially considering the fact that his best football came early in 2025. He trailed off late. If he decides to continue playing, he might as well save his best for the games that matter most. And as we all know, these seasons are marathons. That's what Eric Kendricks did when he signed with the 49ers late last year, and then he ended up sealing the win in the playoffs at Philadelphia with a pass breakup against Jalen Hurts. I could easily see Joey Bosa doing the same thing. Just got married. He could make sure that he's fresh for November and December. He could train in the background, but not abuse his body, and then he can join his brother Nick Bosa if the 49ers get off to a good start and look like they still need just him as that final piece for Super Bowl contention. Back to what Brock Purdy said about Mike Evans. >> Overthrowing him isn't really a thing. >> While I was at tight end you, I made it a point to ask the 49ers in attendance about the impact of this walking Hall of Fame receiver. And Kyle Juszczyk added this. >> Mike Evans I really think he's like no one we've had before. He is so polished, um, has been so dominant in the few practices that we've had him on the field. Uh, is a true difference-maker, and I think it's one that, um, not a lot about it is being talked about, but come [music] season time, like people are going to really see like what a difference this guy can make. Uh, cuz he is a true X receiver that can be singled out by himself, run individual routes, and win against anybody. >> The 49ers have not had a weapon like Mike Evans under Kyle Shanahan. That much is clear. Brock Purdy talking about not being able to overthrow him, Kyle Juszczyk straight up saying that the 49ers have not had a presence like this at the X receiver position. Mac Jones even talked about Mike Evans making a ton of plays over the course of the spring program. >> Mike Evans making plays. >> The truth is that even when Brandon Aiyuk was at his absolute prime for the 49ers, 2.65 yards per route run in 2023 on an absolutely loaded offense, he was not the type of gravitational target with jump ball capabilities that Mike Evans is. And the 49ers now have that. If you're going to focus on the run and leave Mike Evans out on an island, good luck because it's going to be one-on-one and Mike Evans doesn't need speed to beat you one-on-one. That's what the 49ers haven't had. They haven't had true size combined with elite pass-catching ability at the X wide receiver position. That's what Evans brings. That's why Brock Purdy says that he can't overthrow him because the guy gobbles up footballs anywhere in his vicinity. He was making those plays on a consistent basis throughout OTAs and I think that the biggest concern regarding Mike Evans is health. He had those 11 straight 1,000-yard seasons. Only he and Jerry Rice have done that in NFL history, but last year broke the streak. And he dealt with a hamstring injury and I think he dealt with a broken collarbone as well. I mean, it was a rough season for Mike Evans. But the guy has a longer track record of durability and even if he slows down a little bit at age 33, the 49ers can absolutely work with that because he's got other tools in his kit to be a dominant receiver. He's not a receiver who relies solely on burner speed. And guess what? That's why the 49ers also made other moves focused on speed at the wide receiver position. There's De'Johne Strubleling, 436 speed out of Ole Miss. There's Christian Kirk. Times that he posted, three of them, in the playoffs against the Pittsburgh Steelers would have been the fastest miles per hour times posted out of anybody on the 49ers offense last year. And then Kyle Juszczyk also talked about Keelan Black, the rookie running back, and this was unprompted. >> with Strubleling, with Mike Evans, with Christian Kirk, and with Keelan Black. The I I love what I've seen from him. He seems extremely explosive, the guy [music] that can hit home runs. >> It is summer time, which means that it's trip time, which means that it's time to rent a car like this one the good way through Turo. Especially at airports, a whole lot less hassle when you use Turo. With Turo, I can choose the exact car I want, pick it up where it's most convenient for me, and keep it for as long as I need. For anyone traveling soon this summer, Turo is available at over 170 airports across the US and Canada. You can also have it delivered to your home or to your hotel, making Turo super convenient. Rent a summer-ready car, not a rental car, with Turo. Now's a very good time to avoid all those rental car lines. World Cup happening in the US, a lot of visitors everywhere, cramming those airports. We'll skip those lines, get a better car. You can use Turo to do it. This 49ers offense was one of the slowest units in the league last year. They didn't generate separation, and their mph times on average amongst the skill position players were not good. But this season, looks like they can be a whole lot better, and that's outside of Mike Evans. So, Evans is the gravitational force, the contested catchability guy who's going to draw safety attention, create more space, and then the rest of the field can be torched by the burners. That's the idea for the 49ers who finished in the 20s in explosive play rate last season. Kyle Juszczyk explains it well. 49ers were a top five offense last year when it came to overall efficiency. But, there's a difference between a top five offense and a top two offense, and best offense in the league. When the 49ers were the best unit in the league back in 2023, they delivered explosive plays. That's something that the 49ers didn't do last year. the addition of so many wide receivers, especially one who can play Aiyuk's position while Aiyuk is doing who knows what, that can open the 49ers offense up to deliver the explosives that they need. They need more space out on the field, and also ironically, that space can be given by a receiver who can operate without it. Mike Evans' ability to dominate in close quarters is what can open space for the rest of the offense and therefore raise the 49ers explosive play rate. So, buckle your seat belts. It is June 25th. 49ers veterans report to training camp in exactly a month on July 25th. You knock on some wood, you make sure that the health situation stays good, but the team and the roster right now, especially on the offensive side of the ball, seems locked, loaded, ready to go, and address its biggest weakness from Defensively, big picture, well, you look at the fact that they probably still need that one defensive end. I've talked so much about Jadeveon Clowney. Free agent, still out there, could be somebody that the 49ers sign, and we've talked even more about Joey Bosa. Well, think of Joey Bosa as a potential Eric Kendricks reinforcement in 2026. Also, consider the fact that the 49ers have already addressed defensive tackle this offseason with the big trade for Osa Odighizuwa. Chris Kosiorek at the 49ers assistant coach availability talked about how a disruptive interior pass rusher can set the table for everyone else, including defensive ends. >> Yeah, when you when you got a guy inside that can win and and you know, you get him into one-on-one situations and and a guard or a center has to protect against him one-on-one, you know, you anticipate a guy like Osa winning that matchup and you know, when he wins those matchups, he's in a quarterback's lap, he's getting quarterback off the spot, he's you know, he's got a really long wingspan, and he's not the tallest guy in the world, but he's got like an 85-in wingspan that's around the quarterback and it just you know, it sets up things for one, himself, and then two, all the other rushers that, you know, they're coming at the quarterback. Like, if you got an interior rusher from the inside in the quarterback's lap, and he's got to account for that and get off his spot, and next thing you know, his his eyes aren't downfield on receivers, he's looking at the rush. Like, that affects a lot. >> So, Osa bringing over his 52 pressures from Dallas last year to the inside and impressed the 49ers during OTAs. He's there now. 49ers a lot better on the interior. Nick Bosa obviously going to be back off the torn ACL. Well, maybe it just sets the table perfectly for Joey Bosa to swoop in at a time of this season that's beneficial to him. It is a marathon that is run like a sprint, and sometimes you got to run it like a sprint relay. So, maybe 49ers can hand that baton off to Joey Bosa to run the closing leg. Good skilled veterans can often be the cherry on top, and over the course of the next several months between now, June 25th, and December, or maybe even January, we'll keep our eyes open for somebody like Joey Bosa. Could it be a Charles Haley type of signing? Remember back in, what was it? January 1999? Charles Haley had been out of football for 2 years. This was after the Dallas tenure. 49ers signed him just for their post season game against the Green Bay Packers, and they beat the Packers. That was the catch, too, with Terrell Owens. But, in that game, Charles Haley, fresh off the street, 2 years not playing football, I think Joey Bosa would be in a whole lot better shape. Charles Haley forced an interception with a pressure against Brett Favre. The 49ers paid Charles Haley $10,000 to play that game. John Madden said after the play that he earned those $10,000 with his pressure of Brett Favre that turned into a Lee Woodall interception. So, something I'm going to keep an eye on moving forward. Thanks for watching. Hit that sub button. Hit the like button. Those ways you support the channel. We will talk to you very soon.

title: TEU: 🔥49ers CONVENTION — Purdy, Kittle, Mac Jones, Juszczyk
text: You don't normally get this much 49ers news in the dead of the off season, but from the home of the Commodores, we've got a boatload of it. And of course, an epic interview with Mac Jones. >> So, I just did the just straightened up just dead body it. >> And then George put it on his Instagram and it went viral. >> Yeah. Thanks, George. >> Yeah, what does your mom think of your summer haircut? >> Oh, wow. Um she likes it, actually. At first, she hated it. I had to convince her. I started to grow it out more. It's kind of in the awkward stage. Bear with me, people. We'll figure it [laughter] out. Good to see you, David. >> And yes, Mac is fully healthy, throwing the football after not throwing during 49ers OTAs due to a sore shoulder. And we got Brock Purdy, Kyle Juszczyk, and of course, George Kittle, too. >> How are you feeling and are you on track for for week one still? >> Definitely on track. I have a chance. Nothing's 100% certain, but I haven't taken a step back. Nothing's bad has happened. Knock on so much wood. But, um we're slowly getting better. That's all I can ask for. We're pushing it as hard as I can, just without being an idiot. >> Also, a touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Dallas Clark. Where else can you get that? Besides Tight End U. But yes, the day after meeting Baby Lombardi, George Kittle did look great on this field. He obviously still is limited, just crossed 16 mph running. He's going to want to increase that speed by the time that the 49ers season rolls along, but George is optimistic that he can indeed be back very, very early in 2026. The day started in the classroom. It is Tight End University, after all. And George Kittle was the professor. Used some 49ers teach tape. Over 90 tight ends in attendance. This is the biggest the Tight End U has ever been. They actually moved inside the stadium this time. Yes, this is Vanderbilt Stadium here in Nashville. Brock Purdy recently moved to the area. George Kittle's been trying to get him to become tight end U's quarterback or one of the quarterbacks for quite some time. This was the inaugural season of Purdy at tight end U and he mentioned that the move to Nashville, a lot of what was behind it was the opportunity to train with George in the off seasons. >> Yeah, I mean I think that was a huge reason why you know we came out here. Um obviously George, but also the hub of guys that he's, you know, built up with uh training out at his barn on his field and and then specifically throwing to him. Like he's my tight end. So for us to have that chemistry all off season rolling into camp, I thought, you know, last year um you know, going into the season like we were hitting it off really well. So uh we're just going to continue to try to do that. >> A lot of cool 49ers quarterback connections. We saw backups from the entirety of the Kyle Shanahan John Lynch era serve as quarterbacks today in addition obviously to Brock Purdy, the starter, but Brock began as a backup. But you saw the current backup, Mac Jones, more of his interview in a little bit. You saw Brandon Allen, who was with the 49ers a couple seasons ago. Nick Mullens and C.J. Beathard, two former 49ers backups. C.J. lives in this Nashville area. Another cool connection, Shane Wallen, on the 49ers training staff back in 2018. Then he left to the MLB, the Cubs and the Detroit Tigers. Now he's running his own independent shop. He's here in Nashville and he's working with Brock Purdy. So we got to see an old friend, Shane Wallen, out on the field. As I said, year six of tight end U and even Kyle Juszczyk, the fullback, invited this time. And there's so much multi-positional versatility. The cross-training is at an all-time high. You see Kyle Juszczyk actually line up at a tight end position so often. So it's good to have him here and to catch up with him over the course of the afternoon. >> What did it take to to make it to tight end you? >> You know it's funny everyone's like, "Oh, you must be so happy like George finally invited you to tight end you." Um kind of the way it was presented to me is George said, "Hey, Travis would love if you would teach a fullback class at tight end you." >> [laughter] >> So, did Travis invite me or did George invite me? Um doesn't matter. I was excited to finally be out here. It's really cool to hang out with these guys and there's so much overlap between what I do and what tight ends do. So it just makes sense. >> You take about 10 to 15 snaps here out out outside wide receiver. I don't even know how many at tight end, but it's got to be over 100, right? >> Yeah, for sure. >> Given the versatility that you guys run specifically with the 49ers, it's kind of interchangeable skill sets, right? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. I I mean and now it's gotten to the point where like for all of these OTAs, I met with the tight ends. Um because there is there's just so much overlap um and I can learn from what they're being taught. They can learn from what I've been taught from the running back room with Bobby T. Uh so it really is, you know, merging worlds and you're seeing so much around the league where yeah, maybe people don't have fullbacks, but they they have tight ends that play that fullback position. So uh it just makes sense that we're all work together. >> Year 10 for you. You're the longest tenured 49er and you beat George because he was drafted and you signed in March. >> Yep. >> Right? So anyway, George said that you guys didn't become close until probably 2018. He was a rookie in 2017. Do you remember [music] your first interactions with him and how that kind of blossomed in the early years? >> You know it's funny like I don't know if I remember it specifically, but he always tells this story I guess we were on the practice field his rookie year and I remember we were in the Well, I remember a specific play. He was We were in the red zone. He was running like this this fade and he jumped so high and he caught this ball with one hand and I was I was really impressed. Like rookie tight end, looked super athletic, could catch the ball and apparently, I don't remember this part, he came over and I told him that. I'm like, "Hey, like great route." I'm like I'm And I didn't even mean anything by it. I'm like, "What route What round did you get drafted?" He's like, "Oh, fifth round." And I guess I was like, "Okay, cool. I was drafted in the fourth round." And I didn't mean it as like a big bro moment. Like, "Hey, like cool. Like [laughter] good job, but I got drafted before you." But he always likes to remind me of that story. Um questionable if it really happens, but it might have. >> So, he thought he you were big-leaguing him right at the start and maybe that's why the invite was delayed a little. >> Exactly. Exactly. That's why there's the delay for our friendship. >> A lot of really, really good teams, good offenses that you've been on with George. Looking at this season after the pickups, now you've got an X wide receiver who's going to be in the Hall of Fame. They drafted a receiver who can probably play the X too and De'Sean Jackson. Christian Kirk, who you played against, is there. Get Just specifically given how much the receiver position has upgraded, what do you think this offense can do in in 2024? >> I I truly, truly think the sky's the limit. Um I am so excited about those additions. Um Mike Evans I really think he's like no one we've had before. He is so polished, um has been so dominant in the few practices that we've had him on the field, uh is a true difference-maker and I think it's one that um not a lot about it is being talked about, but come season time, like people are going to really see like what a difference this guy can make uh cuz he is a true X receiver that can be singled out by himself, run individual routes, and win against anybody. Uh and then Stribling, I've been so [music] impressed with just how explosive he is, and what a big body he is, and how um intentional he is, and how hard he wants to get involved in the run game. Uh so, for all the success that we had last year with all those injuries, um everything that was stacked against us, quarterbacks moving in and out, and we were still, I believe, [music] like a top-five uh offense. I think if everybody's healthy and those additions, the the sky truly is the limit for us. >> The explosives can be back. >> Explo- And the explosives can return. That's That's what [music] we were missing last year with the explosive plays. Uh and I think we'll we'll have that with with Stribling, with Mike Evans, with Christian Kirk, and with Kaelin Black. The uh I I love what I've seen from him. Uh he seems extremely explosive, [music] a guy that can hit home runs. >> And yes, Brock Purdy was throwing bullets. Here's the full interview with Brock here from Tight End U. >> George finally got you out here? >> Yeah. Oh yeah, he's been hounding me for I think what, 4 years now? So, to be able to come out, um throw the ball around, it's going to be fun. >> George seems like the ultimate peer pressure master based on what I gather. >> Yeah, it's like uh he always pushes, you know, fear of missing out. Like, "Dude, it's going to be fun. It's going to be this and that. And all the things that I've done for you you like." So, like he he puts you in a corner, makes you feel small in a good way, and it's fun. When you get out here, it's worth it. >> You You're out here in the Nashville area. How much work can you end up doing at the barn with him, and how much like route running stuff can you guys get done together? >> Yeah, I mean, I think that was a huge reason why, you know, we came out here. Um obviously, training out at his barn, on his field, him. Like, he's my tight end. So, for us season like we We hitting it really well. So, uh we're just going to continue to try to do that. >> Whoever you got into work with this off-season, I know you got some work in with Mike Evans, but have you been able to to have some of those summits this off-season with your receivers? >> Not yet. We just got out, you know, a couple weeks ago, but we're we're going to have some guys, you know, come together and and you know, get some work in and everything. Obviously, new guys, we want to get the chemistry rolling. I thought we did a good job with that at OTAs, but yeah, we're going to to answer your question, we're going in. >> Biggest thing you've learned from Mike Evans so far? >> Um extremely smart and I feel like overthrowing him isn't really a thing. We saw so many catches in OTAs where he just got up with his length and the radius that he has. You know, he's he's unique, he's a Hall of Famer, and >> [music] >> so yeah. >> Marcos got one. >> Favorite part about being a girl dad? I don't know, there's so many good things. She's growing so fast, but like just holding her and making her laugh, and then when she like pushes off and looks at me and smiles, like seriously, there's nothing better. So. >> And of course, I promised you the Mac Jones interview. Well, he's entertaining as always. How you doing? >> Good. How are you? >> Good summer? >> Very good summer. Very good summer. How about yours? >> Pretty good, pretty good. Uh been in San Francisco hanging out, training and stuff, so. >> You've been in Cabo, too. There's an iconic diving board shot. I I need to know the background on it. [laughter] >> Yeah, so I wasn't going to jump in, it was a little chilly, and then George and Tonz just were like, you have to do it. You got to start this off. So I'm like, if you got if you guys want me to jump, I'll jump, and I can't do a flip, I don't want to get hurt, so I just did the just straightened up just dead bodied it. >> And then George put it on his Instagram, >> Thanks, George. >> There's also something involving like a gong, like you Yeah, that was cool, too. >> Yeah, so that's Deeter's house, and he's the man. He's involved with the 49ers, but he's one of our friends, and he has this gong with the eye shot. I wasn't going to do it, and then again, George is like, you got to do it. So I'm like, all right, so I caught it. Caught it because I wanted to see like how much it weighed and stuff and then ripped it. So, so I caught it video. >> You built a good bond, it seems, with the locker room. How happy are you that no trade, you're back in place with the 49ers this year? >> Oh, it's awesome. I think um the guys on the on the team are awesome. The coaches, support staff, EQ, everybody. And we're all friends, a big family, so if you can be around family, might as well stick around, but you know you know how this business goes. We'll see. >> The 49ers loaded up this season for that offense. You know, Mike Evans is is there and Allen and obviously you're going to hope for better health this year. What do you think this offense can do? >> It's awesome, man. I think Brock's done a great job this offseason just building with the new guys. I've been able to I didn't practice much, but I got to see it all and Mike Evans making plays. A lot of guys that are new, shribbling. Um so, I'm excited. We got We know we got great coaches and players. We just got to be healthy, but if not, we'll figure it out. I feel like that's what we can do. >> Margo, you have one for Mack? >> Uh yeah, what does your mom think of your summer haircut? >> Um she likes it, actually. At first, she of in the awkward stage. So, bear with me, people. We'll figure [laughter] it out. >> Awesome. >> Good to see you. >> And it would not be a proper tight end U without hearing from George Kittle himself, who started this event in 2021 at a local high school. Co-founders, Travis Kelce, obviously very famous, and Greg Olsen, one of the best broadcasters that there is and obviously a grade A tight end back in his playing days. They got some good work in here on the Vanderbilt field. >> How long did it take to get Juice check out? You're like, how long was that a conversation over the past few years? >> Honestly, last year was the first time we asked him, and I'm ashamed it was Travis's idea to invite Juice. Um but Juice didn't want to come because I didn't invite him. So, he's playing hard to get. Um but this year, I asked him probably during the season last year. I was like, "Hey, I need And he's been really excited about it. You know, we're going through the film together, what plays I like, what plays he liked. It's been a really fun to have him here. Just, like I said, his perspective is just so unique. And, like I said, he's the best in the world who's ever done it. So, it's good to hear it. >> You know, it's year 10 for both of you with the 49ers. >> Pretty cool. >> Pretty cool way to to to celebrate that. But, when you look back, meeting Juice the first time, do you remember the first time that you met him in the building in 2017? >> Yeah, we weren't really good friends until like 2018. Took a while. I had to like earn his respect, which I respect from Juice. But, um he's been awesome the entire time. Honestly, my earliest memory of him is him telling me [music] that I was doing a workout wrong in the weight room. I'll never forget it. Thanks, Juice. And I wasn't doing it wrong. You Harvard guys are just so despicable sometimes. But, um he's been awesome. And the cool thing is, too, he's only just gotten better the longer I've been around him. So, that's pretty interesting. >> Brock is here. >> Yes. >> How much did it take to to get Brock to get out to tight end here? >> Um I had to threaten to beat him up. But, he's here. Mac Jones is here. >> We have all former 9ers quarterbacks here today. And it's a I mean, what a great group. They're having a fantastic time. Mac Jones is definitely leading the vibes. Um but, uh Brandon Allen, Nick Mullens are they're striving for second place there. >> And finally, how are you feeling and are you on [music] track for for week one still? Like, nothing's 100% certain, but I haven't taken a step back. Nothing's bad has happened. Knock on so much wood. But, um we're slowly getting better. That's all I can ask for. We're pushing it as hard as I can just without being an idiot. >> The best part of today might have been that we got a break from the excessive Nashville heat. Even some cloud cover right now, but it wasn't all too humid, wasn't all too hot. I think the most pleasant weather conditions that we've ever had at Tight End U. And I've always wanted to check out the newly remodeled Vanderbilt Stadium. That in front of me. We got some luxury suites here now. There's an arms race in college football, and Vanderbilt hosted Tight End U for a few years, but on the practice field, now we are out on the big boy field. And again, I think it's fitting Tight End U's got to happen at an actual university, so Vanderbilt University, the host here in Nashville. But good news all around for the 49ers. George Kittle, we saw him a few months ago, or maybe a month and a half ago in Vegas, looking a little bit slim. He has re-added all the muscle he needs to add. Of course, we saw him moving very well, that video from Brad Graham who did a great job covering this event as well, and now it's just a race against the clock, and the 49ers are going to be back out on their own practice field in about a month. Rookies report for San Francisco on July 18th to training camp, and veterans like George Kittle set to report on July 25th. So, at that point, we'll see where George is at. I would guess he starts training camp on the PUP list, but he can be activated at any time, and they don't play a regular season game until September 11th in Australia. So, this is our big late June / early July event. Tight End U from Nashville getting bigger and bigger every year. This year, we saw plenty of 49ers in attendance, including the QB himself, Brock Purdy, who looked sharp and right into this end zone, he got to throw that touchdown pass to Dallas Clark. Only at Tight End U will you see a connection between a legendary player who's obviously already retired in Dallas Clark and a superstar quarterback like Brock Purdy. But George Kittle organized this back in 2021, and it has really turned into something with a life of its own. Signing off from Nashville, see you next time.
